title: 3.4. Core Issues, Governing Institutions & Governance of IPE
content: 👋 እንኳን ወደ ሶስተኛው ክፍለ-ትምህርት (Section 3.4 & 3.5) በሰላም መጣችሁ! በዚህ ክፍል በ International Political Economy (IPE) ውስጥ ባሉት ዋና ዋና ጉዳዮች (Trade, Investment, Finance)፣ በሚያስተዳድሯቸው ተቋማት (WTO, WB, IMF) እና በ Exchange Rate ሥርዓት ላይ በዝርዝር እናያለን። ተከታተሉኝ👇👇 ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 📌 Overview of IPE Core Issues & Institutions The study of International Political Economy (IPE) revolves around three fundamental pillars: • 1. International Trade (Governed by WTO & Regional FTAs) • 2. International Investment & Transnational Production (Governed by World Bank & TNCs) • 3. International Finance & Exchange Rate Systems (Governed by IMF) 👉 IPE በዋናነት በሦስት ታላላቅ የምጣኔ-ሀብት እና ፖለቲካ ዘርፎች ላይ ያተኩራል፦ ዓለም አቀፍ ንግድ (Trade)፣ ዓለም አቀፍ ኢንቨስትመንት (Investment) እና ዓለም አቀፍ ፋይናንስ (Finance)። እነዚህን እያንዳንዳቸውን ከተቋሞቻቸው ጋር አብረን እንመልከታለን።

title: 3.4.1. International Trade and the WTO
content: 📌 What is International Trade? Most people have a basic understanding of trade, but exchanging a laptop computer for a brand new iPad illustrates barter trade (exchanging goods/services for each other). In the contemporary period, however, the preponderance of trade involves the exchange of money for goods and services. 📌 Domestic vs. Cross-Border Trade • Domestic Trade: Takes place entirely within a single domestic economy. • Cross-Border Trade: Mediated by at least two different national governments, each exercising sovereign authority over its borders. 💡 Critical Insight: Because each national government has its own set of sovereign interests and concerns, even standard "free trade" (*unrestricted purchase and sale of goods and services between countries*) is **never entirely free** in practice. 📌 Scope, Scale & Philosophical Debates Cross-border trade today is immensely greater in scale than at any point in history. • Liberal View: Rejects Autarky (*complete economic self-sufficiency*) as impossible and self-defeating, arguing cross-border trade benefits all nations. • Contrasting Perspectives: - Liberals: Center on the principle of Comparative Advantage. - Mercantilists & Marxists: Center on power differentials between national economies or on class inequality and exploitation. 📌 How is Global Trade Governed? (WTO & NAFTA) Global trade is governed through Global/Regional Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and international bodies like the World Trade Organization (WTO) and NAFTA (North American Free Trade Agreement between U.S., Canada, and Mexico). 📌 The Reality of Free Trade: The Case of NAFTA In NAFTA, "free trade" initially meant a lesser degree of governmental constraints, NOT an elimination of state action. • Tariffs were eliminated by mutual agreement in 2008. • However, Mexico and the U.S. agreed that "import-sensitive sectors" could be protected with emergency safeguard measures if imports caused or threatened serious injury to domestic producers. 📌 Protectionist / Mercantilist Policies Even under free trade regimes, states utilize several protectionist mechanisms: • Tariff: A tax imposed on specific imported goods. • Import Ban: Prohibiting the importation of specific goods. • Import Quota: Quantitative restriction on the amount of goods imported. 💡 Non-Tariff Barriers (NTBs): Import Bans and Quotas are types of NTBs. Other NTBs include domestic health, safety, and environmental regulations, technical standards, and inspection requirements. 📝 Exam Hint: Make sure you can differentiate between Autarky vs. Free Trade, as well as Tariffs (direct tax) and Non-Tariff Barriers (NTBs) (quotas, import bans, safety standards). 👉 ንግድ ማለት የዕቃና አገልግሎት ልውውጥ ነው። የዓለም ንግድ የሚመራው በ WTO እና NAFTA ባሉ ተቋማት ቢሆንም፣ መንግሥታት ሀገር በቀል አምራቾችን ለመጠበቅ Tariff እና Non-Tariff Barriers (NTBs) ይጠቀማሉ።

title: 3.4.2. International Investment and the World Bank
content: 📌 International Investment & Transnational Production (Global FDI) Transnational production is a system where different parts of the overall production process for a single product take place across multiple national territories. 💡 Real-World Example: Swedish Automobile Production A single model of a Swedish car involves at least 38 major and minor components manufactured across factories globally: • Slovakia (Klüster): Hood latch cable • Japan (Alpine & Sanden): Amplifier and Turbo diesel • USA (BorgWarner & GKN/Visteon): Engine control unit and Drive shaft • France (Valeo): Air conditioner | Germany (Brose): Doors • Other contributors: Norway, Brazil, Canada, Holland, UK, and Sweden. 📌 Why Transnational Production Networks Expanded 1. Drastic decrease in transport and communications costs (making global production efficient). 2. Rise of efficiency-seeking FDI (Foreign Direct Investment). 3. New and better technologies and global financial improvements. 📌 Divergent Investment Governance • Developed Countries: Investment and development processes are predominantly governed by the interactions of Multinational Corporations (MNCs/TNCs). • Developing Countries: Directly or indirectly governed by the World Bank (WB)—sometimes holding more power than sovereign states. 📌 Origin and Evolution of the World Bank • Original Purpose: Created post-WWII as a vehicle for disbursing Marshall Plan money to aid the reconstruction of Europe. • Expansion: Later expanded its scope to developing countries in Asia, Africa, and Latin America. 📌 The Controversial Impact on Developing Nations Unlike its success in Europe, the World Bank's impact in developing nations has been controversial or negative due to: 1. "One size fits all" policy prescriptions: Mandating excessive, standardized neo-liberal policies. 2. Tough Aid/Loan Conditions: Enforcing strict policy conditions that infringe upon the national policy freedom of sovereign states. 📝 Exam Hint: Understand that Global FDI is driven by reduced transport/communication costs, and be ready to compare the World Bank's initial role in Europe (Marshall Plan) with its controversial "one-size-fits-all" neoliberal conditionality in developing nations. 👉 Transnational Production (Global FDI) ማለት የአንድን ምርት የተለያዩ ክፍሎች በተለያዩ ሀገራት ማምረት ነው። በበለፀጉ ሀገራት ሂደቱን TNCs ሲመሩት፣ ታዳጊ ሀገራት ላይ ግን World Bank በ "One size fits all" ፖሊሲዎቹ እና በብድር መስፈርቶቹ ከፍተኛ ተፅዕኖ ያሳድራል።

title: 3.4.3. International Finance and the IMF
content: 📌 The Global Financial System Structure The global financial system is divided into two separate, but tightly interrelated systems: 1. The International Monetary System: • Defines the relationship between and among national currencies. • Revolves around how the exchange rate among different national currencies is determined. 2. The Credit System: • The framework of rules, agreements, institutions, and practices that facilitate the transnational flow of financial capital for investment and trade financing. 💡 System Interdependence: The monetary system regulates currency pricing, while the credit system regulates capital movement—making them inextricably linked. 📝 Exam Hint: Be prepared to define and distinguish between the International Monetary System (exchange rates/currencies) and the Credit System (flow of financial capital/loans). 👉 የዓለም አቀፍ ፋይናንስ ሥርዓት በሁለት የተሳሰሩ ክፍሎች ይከፈላል፦ Monetary System (በሀገራት ገንዘቦች/Currency መካከል ያለውን የምንዛሬ ተመን የሚያጠና) እና Credit System (ለኢንቨስትመንትና ንግድ የሚሆን የገንዘብ ካፒታል ዝውውርን የሚያመቻች)።

title: 3.5. Exchange Rates and the Exchange-Rate System
content: 📌 What is an Exchange Rate? An exchange rate is the price of one national currency in terms of another. 💡 Real-World Numerical Example (Module Data): • August 1998: $1 USD = 145.8 Japanese Yen (¥) • July 2013: $1 USD = 98.1 Japanese Yen (¥) • Analysis: The Yen was nearly 50% **weaker** in 1998 compared to 2013. • Purchasing Power Impact: $2,000 USD exchanged for 291,000 Yen in 1998, but only 196,000 Yen in 2013. You got far less Yen in 2013. 📌 Two Main Exchange Rate Systems • 1. Pure Floating-Rate System: Value is determined solely by market supply and demand without any government intervention. • 2. Pure Fixed-Rate System: Value is pegged/fixed against another single currency or a basket of currencies. 📌 Governance of Global Finance: The IMF The International Monetary Fund (IMF) was created to govern the global financial system. Although set up as an ostensibly neutral institution, it was designed to represent U.S. power and interests first, and major developed capitalist countries secondarily. 📌 Decision-Making and the Quota System Unlike "one-country, one-vote" political assemblies, voting power within the IMF is determined by a country's Quota. • What is a Quota? Capital subscription (the amount of money) paid by a member country to the IMF. • Power Distribution: The more money a country pays, the more voting power and decision-making influence it commands. • Dominance: The United States holds the top quota share, giving it dominant sway over IMF operations. 📝 Exam Hint: Remember: Floating Rate = Market Supply/Demand; Fixed Rate = Pegged Value. Also note that decision-making power in the IMF is determined by a country's Quota, NOT by equal voting. 👉 የምንዛሬ ተመን (Exchange Rate) በFloating እና Fixed ሥርዓቶች የሚመራ ሲሆን፣ ዓለም አቀፍ የፋይናንስ ሥርዓቱን የሚያስተዳድረው IMF ደግሞ በ "Quota" (የካፒታል መጠን) መሠረት አሜሪካን ከፍተኛ የበላይነት እንዲኖራት አድርጓል።

title: Chapter 3 Core Summary: Governing IPE Matrix
content: 📌 Summary Matrix of Core IPE Issues & Institutions | IPE Core Issue | Core Focus | Governing Body / System | Key Governance Feature | |---|---|---|---| | International Trade | Goods & Services Exchange | WTO & FTAs (NAFTA) | Tariff reductions, NTBs, Safeguard measures | | International Investment | Transnational Production / FDI | World Bank & TNCs | Marshall Plan roots, Neoliberal conditionality | | International Finance | Monetary & Credit Systems | IMF | Exchange rate systems, Quota-based voting | ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 📝 Exam Hint: Memorize this table! Exam questions often ask you to match the core IPE issue (Trade, Investment, Finance) with its primary governing institution (WTO, World Bank, IMF). 👉 በአጠቃላይ ምዕራፍ 3ን ለማጠቃለል፦ ንግድ በ WTO፣ ኢንቨስትመንት በ World Bank እና TNCs፣ ፋይናንስ ደግሞ በ IMF እና በ Quota ሥርዓት ይመራሉ። እነዚህን የሰንጠረዥ ግንኙነቶች ማወቅ ለፈተናችሁ በጣም ይረዳችኋል። ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🙏 የዚህ ምዕራፍ ትምህርት በዚሁ ተጠናቋል! በቀጣይ ምዕራፍ 4 እንቀጥላለን። ደህና ሁኑ!
